messages.text: Weekly vuln scan results are in. 3 criticals, 11 highs across prod. Biggest cluster is on DocVault app nodes, looks like an outdated image library. Ticket incoming.
Is that the same libxml-ish finding from two weeks ago or a new CVE? We patched DocVault in July.
New one. Different CVE, same base image. The July patch bumped the OS packages but the image processing lib got pinned by the Dockerfile. Fix is probably a one-line version bump.
Fwiw I can take the DocVault bump if someone reviews. Need to check the thumbnail service doesn't break on the newer lib version.
I'll review. Ping me when the PR is up. Please run the doc upload integration suite against staging, not just unit tests.
Will do. Staging first, then we schedule prod for the Tuesday window unless it's exploitable externally.
It's behind AuthSSO and not internet-facing, so CVSS environmental score drops to medium-ish. Tuesday window is fine, but I'll still flag it in the exception tracker.
Any DataLake findings in the scan? I saw the Spark nodes got flagged last quarter for an old log4j-adjacent dependency.
2 highs on DataLake. One is the Jupyter gateway running an unsupported version, the other is a TLS config on the metastore. Neither is critical. Sending you the report.
Got it. Jupyter gateway upgrade has been on my list anyway. I can do the metastore TLS change this week, it's a config flag plus restart. Restart will pause ingestion jobs for ~10 min.
Quick question, are the 11 highs deduped? Last time the scanner counted the same package once per container and inflated the number.
Good catch, raw count was 11 but deduped by package and CVE it's closer to 6 unique. I'll update the summary so nobody panics in the leadership readout.
Nice. I can take two of the remaining unique ones if they're app dependencies. Send me the list and I'll open PRs this afternoon.
Summary posted in the ticket with owners assigned: Travis on DocVault, Michael on DataLake, Kevin on the two app deps. Target is everything closed or excepted by end of next week.
